title: P/Invoke awareness without becoming a C++ shop
hook: P/Invoke is how managed code calls a native export. It is a marshalling and lifetime problem. It is not a request to rewrite the worker in C++.

sections.heading: The boundary, not the language
sections.prose: A P/Invoke declares a native entry point, a calling convention, and how each argument becomes bits the other ABI understands. Strings, bools, and structs are where people lose days. You need to know: who allocates, who frees, whether the native API expects UTF-16 or UTF-8, and whether the handle is an `IntPtr` you must `Dispose`. SkiaSharp (and similar) wrap that handle in a managed object with `Dispose` — forgetting `using` leaks native heaps the CLR GC will never see. That is module 06’s `IDisposable` with teeth. You do not need to recite `stdcall` versus `cdecl` unless the signature is wrong; you need to own the wrapper project so the rest of the solution stays safe C#.

snippets.label: LibraryImport instead of a hand-rolled DllImport stub
snippets.explanation: LibraryImport is a source generator (module 16). The method is partial, the project allows unsafe blocks, marshalling is generated at compile time — including Native AOT — instead of a runtime IL stub from DllImport.

sections.heading: Span versus Memory at the native edge
sections.prose: Microsoft’s memory guidelines: wrap a synchronous native call with `Span<T>` (and `fixed` or generated marshalling). Wrap an asynchronous native call with `Memory<T>` and `Memory<T>.Pin`, because `fixed` cannot span an `await`. Never pass a pinned span without a length if the native side might walk until `\0`. Prefer letting `LibraryImport` marshal `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` when the generator supports it. If the native library is a RabbitMQ C client you should not have chosen, stop — use the managed client. P/Invoke is for the library you cannot avoid (codec, OS, vendor SDK), not for fashion.

snippets.label: Wrong: span as a C string
snippets.explanation: The unsafe best-practices doc calls this out explicitly. Interviews like this because it shows you have read the boundary rules, not a C++ textbook.

sections.heading: What this track will not teach
sections.prose: This is not COM, C++/CLI, or how to write a vtable. If an interviewer dives into `MarshalAs`, answer with “I would look up the library’s ABI, generate LibraryImport, write interop tests, and keep the unsafe project tiny.” Then steer to lifetime: `IDisposable`, pinning duration, and AOT. Seniority here is containment.

interviewTakeaways: P/Invoke is marshalling plus lifetime; prefer LibraryImport source generation over DllImport.
Synchronous native wrappers take Span; asynchronous ones take Memory and Pin.
Native handles need Dispose; the CLR will not collect a SkiaSharp-style unmanaged heap for you.
commonPitfalls: Calling DllImport with CharSet mismatches and blaming the native vendor.
Pinning a buffer for the lifetime of a request instead of for the native call.
Spreading AllowUnsafeBlocks and native types into domain assemblies.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node native addons and bun:ffi are the same class of problem: ABI, strings, and who frees. JS still does not pin interior pointers the way fixed does.
